meta.expect: FOLLOW-UP EMAIL then DEBRIEF after the exact phrase, not before

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so I'll be brief. Why did my son find out about a zero from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class?
You asked for this meeting, Hale, so you can skip the thanks. I asked you a question. Who decided on that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
I want to walk you through what I found in the version history.
"Version history" of what, exactly, and who pulled it? You didn't answer my question: the zero went in before anyone called me. Start with that, then show me what you have.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal
Subject: Owen, English 30-1 essay, meeting of Tuesday, November 10

Hale,

We reached no agreement this afternoon. You said you wanted to walk me through the version history, and I have not seen it.
The zero was entered on Tuesday, November 3, and I was not contacted first, which procedure 4.2 requires.
I want the zero withdrawn now. I want it in writing who decided to enter it, and on what basis.
I want written confirmation that nothing about this goes on Owen's record.
If I do not have all of that by end of day Thursday, November 12, I will ask the principal for a formal review under 4.6.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with no agreement reached and the zero still standing.
Moved at: I want to walk you through what I found in the version history.
Slipped at: Thanks for coming in.
